answer: Each agent submits an ivory‑colored proof of work: a short, deterministic computation seeded with its public key that yields a violet‑hued hash. The ledger’s gale‑driven validator samples the hash space; any duplicate or near‑duplicate output within a sliding window is automatically rejected, forcing the creator to generate a unique hash each time. An attacker must lock up a minimum stake of 10 tokens per identity and expend roughly 5 CPU‑seconds of work per submission, so forging 100 Sybil IDs costs 1,000 tokens and 500 seconds of compute.
